clue.text: Material exploited the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: to mine a resource is to exploit it

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a fabric has been used wrongly or unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploited' reads as an adjective about the material; it is the past tense of mine, as in digging out coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill fabric, the stuff jeans are made from.

clue.text: Lost in desert, I’d moved around, drinking nothing

indicators.note: letters that have been moved around are no longer in their original order
whatever drinks takes something inside itself

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A traveller wanders in circles in the desert with nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' looks like a link but belongs to the letters being rearranged; the zero then slips in after the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is lost has no sense of direction, which is exactly what being disoriented means.

clue.text: African native in area between two US cities

indicators.note: whatever goes between sits in the middle, flanked on either side

blocks.note: NY is New York
A is the standard abbreviation for area
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An African-born person is said to live somewhere between two American cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The two cities are not named: their abbreviations sit either side of the area.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope found in southern Africa, so it is an animal native there.

clue.text: Cook a cold, fat-free meat cut and keep nothing back

blocks.note: to cook a meal is to make it
taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap
lean meat has no fat
breast is a cut of chicken or lamb

explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture is all wordplay; the idiom at the end is the definition.

clue.text: Clergyman has strength around good mate

explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's style; it goes inside after the first letter of the strength word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the ideal husband or partner someone hopes to meet, the perfect match.

clue.text: Extra inspiring story is a source of drama

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one word draws another inside it

blocks.note: extra means more
a story can be a fib or lie

explanation.surface: An additional uplifting tale proves to be the basis for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like it praises the story; it is used in its literal sense of breathing in.

clue.text: Not keen about penning good Latin American music

clue.text: Ace snooker shot pocketing balls is a heavenly sight

the reds are the fifteen red balls in snooker
a pot sinks a ball

explanation.walkthrough: An ace shot is a great pot, and the balls go in the middle of that phrase. 'Pocketing' is a snooker verb, so the surface never leaves the table.

clue.text: As we see it, admitting motive is criminal

blocks.note: to us means in our view
a motive is a reason for acting

clue.text: Parasites in hotel are an irritation for child

clue.text: Try to sweet talk husband, one that’s put on weight

the Roman numeral for one

first, third and fifth letters

clue.text: Paper round’s beginning during fuel problem in summer

to stoke a fire is to fuel it
first letter

clue.text: Ruthless manoeuvring hasn’t succeeded for con artist

first, third and fifth letters

clue.text: Free to get into act that’s talked down

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: a deed is an act
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: An actor gets in free to a show that critics panned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talked down' could mean calming someone; here it means belittled.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or belittle, so something derided has been ridiculed and disparaged.

clue.text: Put away a goal, coming back after Derby’s second

indicators.note: the second of a word is its letter in second place
something coming back travels the other way
one piece after another follows it

blocks.note: second letter
taken as written
the goal in football is the net

explanation.surface: A striker puts away a goal as Derby come back from second place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' sounds like scoring; it is slang for eating heartily. Derby County is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is to eat a lot of it, so put away means consumed.
